facts.text: Qualitative off-road evidence reports that underground coal workers change where they stand and how they work, remove tags, ask for bypasses, and report distraction.

facts.text: The passenger-car results from the USA and Japan are comparison-only evidence, not evidence about mining operators, because on-road drivers face different speeds, road rules, obstacle distributions, vehicle dynamics, and task objectives.

facts.text: An IIHS study by Cicchino in 2019 found that rear automatic braking with a camera and sensors reduced passenger-car backing crash involvement by 78%, compared with 42% for a camera plus sensors without braking; this is independent on-road evidence.
facts.quote: Rear automatic braking with camera and sensors cut backing crash involvement by 78%, against 42% for camera plus sensors without braking (IIHS, Cicchino, 2019) [24].

facts.text: Cicchino's 2017 on-road study found that front FCW plus AEB reduced rear-end striking crashes by 50%.
facts.quote: Front FCW plus AEB cut rear-end striking crashes by 50% (Cicchino, 2017) [23].

facts.text: An IIHS study by Cox, Reagan and Cicchino in 2025 found that on-road drivers keep prevention systems switched on more than warning-only systems.
facts.quote: Drivers keep prevention systems switched on more than warning-only systems: 93% had AEB enabled, while lane departure systems were enabled less often (IIHS, Cox, Reagan and Cicchino, 2025) [25].

facts.text: An IIHS study by Cox, Reagan and Cicchino in 2025 found that 93% of on-road drivers had AEB enabled, while lane departure systems were enabled less often.
facts.quote: 93% had AEB enabled, while lane departure systems were enabled less often (IIHS, Cox, Reagan and Cicchino, 2025) [25].

facts.text: A Japanese simulator study published in Human Factors in 2020 found that drivers who trusted other vehicles' AEB braked later.
facts.quote: In a simulator study, drivers who trusted other vehicles' AEB braked later (Japan, Human Factors, 2020).

facts.text: The Japanese 2020 simulator finding that drivers trusting other vehicles' AEB braked later represents negative behavioral adaptation by people who do not use the system and is a possible parallel for ground crew around automatically braking machines.
facts.quote: This is negative behavioral adaptation by people who do not use the system, a possible parallel for ground crew around machines that brake automatically [26].
